title: Slice restriction commutes with total derived inverse limit of strict towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal A_U=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O|_U)$ on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $j_U^*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A_U$ be restriction and let $j_U^{*,\operatorname{Tow}}$ apply it levelwise to $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, with levelwise exactness. Both restrictions induce termwise functors on unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $L_{\mathcal A}$ and $L_{\mathcal A_U}$ for total right derived inverse limit, computed by a K-injective resolution of strict towers followed by termwise inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$j_U^*L_{\mathcal A}(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal A_U}(j_U^{*,\operatorname{Tow}}X)$$
for every $X\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$. It is the derived comparison induced by the underived restriction/limit comparison and commutes with each tower projection. In particular it identifies the derived limit of the multiplication-by-$a$ tower of any $H\in D(\mathcal A)$, restricted to $U$, with the derived limit of the multiplication-by-$a|_U$ tower of $H|_U$, for every global section $a$ of $\mathcal O$.

proof.text: Write $j=j_U^*$ and $E=j_{U!}$. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], $E\dashv j$ and both functors are exact. Define $E^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ by applying $E$ to each term and transition. The componentwise adjunction bijections identify tower maps $E^{\operatorname{Tow}}T\to S$ with tower maps $T\to j^{\operatorname{Tow}}S$: naturality of the bijection changes the equation for each transition on one side into the equation on the other. Hence $E^{\operatorname{Tow}}\dashv j^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. Both are additive and exact, since addition and exactness are levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Exactness preserves $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$, so $j$ and $j^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce the termwise derived functors in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); componentwise lift of the adjunction to strict towers

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to the additive adjunction $E^{\operatorname{Tow}}\dashv j^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ of Step 1, whose left adjoint is exact. It follows that if $I$ is a K-injective complex of strict towers, then $j^{\operatorname{Tow}}I$ is K-injective as a complex of strict towers on $\mathcal C/U$. This is K-injectivity in the whole tower category, rather than just K-injectivity of each evaluated complex.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), applied to the two abelian tower categories

proof.text: For a tower of module sheaves $T$, its ordinary limit is the sheaf assigning to $V$ the compatible tuples $(t_n)$ in $\prod_n T_n(V)$. Indeed a matching family of compatible tuples glues coordinate by coordinate; uniqueness of gluing makes the glued coordinates satisfy each transition equation. This gives the limit universal property for module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restriction is sectionwise by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Therefore on $V\to U$ both $j(\lim T)$ and $\lim(j^{\operatorname{Tow}}T)$ are precisely those tuples in $\prod_nT_n(V)$. The identity on tuples gives a natural isomorphism $c_T:j\lim T\to\lim j^{\operatorname{Tow}}T$. It commutes with projections and with differentials when $T$ is a tower complex.

source.place: Tag 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site), rule j_U^*F(V/U)=F(V); sectionwise compatible-tuple calculation

proof.text: Represent $X$ by a tower complex and take a K-injective tower resolution $q:X\to I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then $L_{\mathcal A}(X)$ is represented by $\lim I$. Step 1 makes $j^{\operatorname{Tow}}q$ a quasi-isomorphism, and Step 2 makes its target K-injective. The same cited strict-tower model on the small slice site thus computes $L_{\mathcal A_U}(j^{\operatorname{Tow}}X)$ by $\lim j^{\operatorname{Tow}}I$. Exactness of $j$ computes the other side by $j\lim I$. Apply $c_I$ of Step 3 to obtain the asserted isomorphism. It uses the original coefficient ring restricted to the slice, with no change of coefficients.

source.place: Tags 0940 (section-derived-limits) and 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective strict-tower computation on C and C/U

proof.text: This construction is canonical on the derived tower category. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], a morphism between two objects is represented by a unique homotopy class of maps between their chosen K-injective tower representatives. The isomorphisms $c_I$ commute with these maps by the tuple formula of Step 3. Applying either restriction or inverse limit to the equations defining a chain homotopy again gives those equations, since both functors are additive. Thus the construction respects the representing homotopy classes and is natural on the derived category. Replacing a K-injective representative uses a homotopy equivalence by that same cited statement; the naturality equation identifies the two constructions. On a K-injective representative its map is exactly the underived comparison $c_I$, so this is the derived comparison specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), Hom bijection and homotopy-equivalence comparison; applied to tower categories

proof.text: For each $n$, the projection is represented by $\lim I\to I_n$. To view its target as $X_n$, invert the evaluated resolution map $q_n:X_n\to I_n$, which is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The tuple formula gives $\operatorname{pr}_n\,c_I=j(\operatorname{pr}_n)$, with source $j\lim I$; exact restriction also inverts $j(q_n)$. This proves compatibility with every derived tower projection. Finally, for a representative $H^\bullet$ of $H$, multiplication by a global $a$ defines a strict tower complex. A different representative is connected through quasi-isomorphisms, which are levelwise quasi-isomorphisms of these towers, so its derived tower is well defined. Sectionwise restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] sends each transition $a:H^\bullet\to H^\bullet$ to multiplication by $a|_U$. Applying Steps 4–5 to this tower proves the final assertion with its actual scalar transitions.
